about: Every publication this project prepares, and where each one stands. docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md explains the steps and the statuses; node tools/paper-check.js checks each entry against its files, and allows no email address in a paper's files except author.email. Update this file in the pull request that changes a status.

papers.title: Minimal Winding in the Self-Similar Collapse of Point Vortices

papers.title: Stable Self-Similar Expansion of Four and Five Point Vortices and Confinement of Vortex Patches
papers.note: Drafted in this repository by the owner's decision (2026-09-25): computer-assisted proof that four and five Euler vortices have self-similarly expanding configurations that are stable modulo rotation and their family, linearly and nonlinearly (orbital asymptotic stability with the rate 1/size, the limit fixed by the energy, and an a priori estimate for forced motions), and Zbarsky's vortex-patch confinement theorem carried over to them. By the owner's decision (2026-09-25) it gets its first release in its companion repository, archived on Zenodo for a DOI, once its quality record is complete. Theorem 4 is proved in full in Appendix A (2026-09-26); independent readings of every section and of the programs are recorded in notes/QUALITY.md with their fixes; the owner signed off and the quality bar is met (2026-09-26). papers.title: Hopf Bifurcations and Bistability in the Hodgkin-Huxley Equations at the 1952 Parameters: Computer-Assisted Proofs
papers.note: Computer-assisted proofs, for every leak potential in [10.59, 10.62], of the unique equilibrium for J in [0, 200], its two Hopf points (subcritical and supercritical, first Lyapunov coefficients enclosed) and bistability of rest and repetitive firing at J = 8. Six in-project readings by separate agents (2026-09-27), every must-fix finding fixed (notes/referee-2026-09-27-*.md), and a mutation study of the programs (data/mutation_study.txt). Du and Hassard (2001) computed Hopf coefficients of the model in interval arithmetic; only its first page could be read, and no priority is claimed for the equilibria, the Hopf points or their criticality. papers.title: Chaos and Analytic Non-Integrability of the Classical Double Pendulum: A Computer-Assisted Proof
papers.note: Drafted in this repository by the owner's standing decision (2026-09-26) from research/double-pendulum/: a computer-assisted proof (CAPD, interval arithmetic) that the equal double pendulum has a hyperbolic periodic orbit with a transversal homoclinic orbit at E = -1/2, 0, 1/2 and for every E in [-1e-10, 1e-10], hence no analytic invariant function on these levels and no real-analytic integral independent of the energy near the level E = 0; explicit topological horseshoes from covering relations at E = -1/2, 0, 1/2 (entropy above 0.0906, 0.1016, 0.0906 per return); Smale's 1965 proof does not apply as written to an area-preserving map, and later forms of the Smale-Birkhoff theorem (not read here, not used) are discussed in Remark 2. Novelty checks of 2026-09-27 (RESEARCH.md): Szuminski and Kapitaniak (2025) read in full, no newer proof found; Bolotin and Negrini (1997) known only from search snippets, so the novelty of global non-integrability and of chaos in the equal case is stated conditionally, and the printed pages to obtain are listed in research/double-pendulum/BOLOTIN-NEGRINI.md. The local unstable manifold and the local lambda-lemma are proved in the paper from certified cone conditions (Lemmas 5 and 8), so no theorem stated for diffeomorphisms of a whole manifold is applied to the return map. An in-project adversarial reading (notes/review-1.md, verdict minor revision) found one must-fix (a hypothesis checked by no program, now checked by code/cones.cpp) and should-fix items, all fixed and answered in its Response section; the quality bar is met (notes/QUALITY.md). On 2026-09-29 the whole of run_all.sh was run again against CAPD at the pinned commit 03dc562, on two threads, in 39 minutes: every proof passed, every control failed for its stated reason, and the reports match the committed files except for the order of parallel lines in E0.txt and E0_interval.txt. The Arb cross-checks were run again the same day and match the committed reports apart from their times. Release 1.0.0 is in the companion repository ChaseHendrick/double-pendulum, archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.22997540 (2026-09-27). Meromorphic non-integrability remains open. No outside review. No journal chosen. Release 1.0.1, the checking release, is archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23028523 (2026-09-29). Release 1.0.0 remains doi:10.5281/zenodo.22997540. papers.title: Traveling Pulses in a Neural Field with a Smooth Firing Rate: Computer-Assisted Existence and Spectral Stability
papers.note: Ready (2026-09-27): the quality record, notes/QUALITY.md, is complete. Drafted in this repository by the owner's decision (2026-09-26): computer-assisted proofs in ball arithmetic of traveling pulses of the Pinto-Ermentrout neural field with a logistic firing rate at explicit, non-small recovery rates (a fast and a slow pulse at eps = 1/10 and 3/20, a fast pulse on [0.08, 0.13693] and five further intervals, the Fig. 5 sigmoid of Pinto and Ermentrout, Faye's model with synaptic depression at eps = 1/100, 1/50 and 1/20) and spectral stability of the fast pulse at eps = 1/10; nonlinear stability not proved (39 pages). The programs and certificates are in papers/nf-pulse/ (code/, ext/); every check script was rerun on 2026-09-27 with the present programs (review/RERUNS.md). All checks were made within the project by separate AI agent sessions, none of them an outside review: review/, ext/*/REPORT.md, three readings of the manuscript on 2026-09-27, then a fourth and a fifth reading of the proofs written in response and a review of the stability controls, with a response to each finding in notes/referee-2026-09-27-*.md. Enculescu (2004) could not be reached and is unread, and Sandstede (2007) is known from its abstract only; the manuscript says what the works read contain and makes no claim to be first. papers.title: Stable Rotating Waves in Rings of a Modified Ventricular Myocyte Model Near a Hopf Point: Computer-Assisted Proofs in Fourier Space
papers.note: Drafted in this repository by the owner's standing decision (2026-09-26) from research/cardiac-cycle-certificates/, the canonical location of its programs and records (the copies in code/ and data/ are byte-identical, and the records' hashes refer to paths relative to that folder). Computer-assisted proofs for Erhardt's 18-state modification of the TP06 endocardial cell at G_Ks = 0.0275: the cell's periodic orbit by CAPD (patched 6.1.0) and, independently, in Fourier space with Arb; and rotating 1-waves in rings of N = 8, 16, 32, 64 cells with existence, local uniqueness, minimal period and local exponential orbital stability (all 18N - 1 nontrivial Floquet multipliers below e^(-delta T), delta = 5e-6 per ms). The programs and the stability lemmas had in-project adversarial readings by separate AI agent sessions, with a second reading of the fixes (review/); no reader has yet been briefed with the manuscript, and there has been no outside review. Identification with Erhardt's Hopf branch is numerical. The G_Ks branch (rec 2) is in progress and not part of this draft. No PDF yet (no TeX toolchain where it was drafted); quality items 1, 4, 6 and 7 are open (notes/QUALITY.md). No journal chosen.
